title: Daily weather pipeline, line by line
subtitle: One run on 1 October 2026 with --full-refresh: readings in, a cleaned daily summary, a report, a table and an alert out.

main.py:2.title: Import the tools and the settings
main.py:2.text: argparse, logging and datetime.date come from the standard library. The last import pulls INPUT_CSV and STATIONS_DB from config: the first import of a module executes it from the top, so the walkthrough steps into config.py before these names are bound.

config.py:4.title: Define the pipeline's constants
config.py:4.text: Module-level constants: input and output locations, and the thresholds used later. MIN_TEMP_C and MAX_TEMP_C bound physically plausible readings; ANOMALY_Z is the z-score cut-off for flagging a station.

config.py:10.title: Read the webhook URL from the environment
config.py:10.text: os.getenv returns the ALERT_WEBHOOK environment variable if it is set, otherwise the default URL. The variable wasn't set in this run, so the default was used.

config.py:11.title: Read the API token from the environment
config.py:11.text: Same pattern as the webhook. The default is a hard-coded token, which is a security smell: a real secret should never be committed as a fallback. codestory masks its value.

main.py:7.title: Import the extract functions
main.py:7.text: Importing etl.extract runs that module: it imports sqlite3 and pandas and defines read_readings and load_stations, which this line then binds here.

etl/clean.py:4.title: Define the cleaning steps
etl/clean.py:4.text: Four plain functions that each take a DataFrame and return a new one, so they can be chained. clean() composes the other three.

main.py:12.title: Configure logging
main.py:12.text: basicConfig installs a root handler that prints just the message text at INFO level and above. It only has an effect the first time it's called in a process.

main.py:45.title: Run main() only when executed as a script
main.py:45.text: __name__ is "__main__" when the file is run directly (or through runpy, as codestory does), and the module's name when it's imported. This guard keeps imports side-effect free.

main.py:25.title: Parse the command line
main.py:25.text: parse_args() builds the parser and returns an argparse.Namespace; args.date and args.full_refresh are read later to name the report and decide whether to clear the table.

main.py:21.title: Return the parsed options
main.py:21.text: parse_args() with no argument reads sys.argv[1:]. codestory set sys.argv to this run's arguments, so the Namespace holds date=2026-10-01 and full_refresh=True.

main.py:26.title: Load the raw readings
main.py:26.text: Calls read_readings with the CSV path from config and binds the resulting DataFrame to raw.

etl/extract.py:7.title: Read the CSV into a DataFrame
etl/extract.py:7.text: pd.read_csv parses the file into a DataFrame; parse_dates converts the timestamp column to datetime64 so the .dt accessor works later. 601 rows, 4 columns: station_id, timestamp, temp, unit.

main.py:27.title: Load the station metadata
main.py:27.text: Calls load_stations with the SQLite path and binds the 12-row station table to stations.

etl/extract.py:13.title: Open the stations database
etl/extract.py:13.text: sqlite3.connect opens the file; as a context manager the connection commits (or rolls back on error) when the block exits. Note that it does not close the connection. In safe mode, codestory pointed this at a copy of the database.

etl/extract.py:14.title: Query the stations table
etl/extract.py:14.text: pd.read_sql_query runs the SELECT on the open connection and returns the result as a DataFrame: 12 stations with name, region and elevation.

main.py:30.title: Clean the readings
main.py:30.text: Passes the raw DataFrame through clean(), which applies three cleaning functions in sequence and returns the result as readings.

etl/clean.py:25.title: Apply each cleaning step in order
etl/clean.py:25.text: Iterates over a tuple of functions. Functions are first-class values, so step is bound to to_celsius, then drop_invalid, then dedupe; static analysis can't see these calls, which is why codestory records them at run time.

etl/clean.py:26.title: Replace df with the step's output
etl/clean.py:26.text: Calls the current step and rebinds df to the returned DataFrame. Each step returns a new object rather than mutating its argument, so raw is left untouched.

etl/clean.py:6.title: Copy before modifying
etl/clean.py:6.text: df.copy() makes an independent DataFrame, so the in-place assignments below don't modify the caller's object (and avoid pandas' SettingWithCopy warning).

etl/clean.py:7.title: Mark the Fahrenheit rows
etl/clean.py:7.text: A vectorised comparison that produces a boolean Series aligned to df's index: True for rows whose unit is "F".

etl/clean.py:8.title: Convert those rows to Celsius
etl/clean.py:8.text: df.loc[f, "temp"] selects the temp column for the masked rows only, and assigns the converted values back in place. Rows already in Celsius are untouched.

etl/clean.py:9.title: Label every row as Celsius
etl/clean.py:9.text: Broadcasts the scalar "C" to the whole unit column, now that all temperatures are in Celsius.

etl/clean.py:15.title: Drop rows with missing values
etl/clean.py:15.text: dropna with subset only considers temp and station_id: a row is removed if either is NaN. 19 rows go, leaving 582.

etl/clean.py:16.title: Keep plausible temperatures
etl/clean.py:16.text: Builds a boolean mask from two comparisons combined with & (element-wise and; the parentheses are required because & binds tighter than >=), then indexes df with it. The sensor glitches reading 999 are removed: 576 rows remain.

etl/clean.py:21.title: Remove resent readings
etl/clean.py:21.text: drop_duplicates on station_id and timestamp keeps the first occurrence of each pair. 24 duplicates go: 576 rows become 552.

main.py:31.title: Join station details, then summarise
main.py:31.text: Nested calls are evaluated inside-out: enrich(readings, stations) runs first, and its result is passed straight to daily_summary. Only the final summary is bound to a name.

etl/transform.py:7.title: Left-join the station table
etl/transform.py:7.text: merge on station_id with how="left" keeps every reading and adds name, region and elevation_m from the matching station. Row count is unchanged (552) because station_id is unique in stations; columns go from 4 to 7.

etl/transform.py:12.title: Add a calendar-day column
etl/transform.py:12.text: assign returns a new DataFrame with an extra column; .dt.date extracts the date part of each timestamp, giving the grouping key for daily figures.

etl/transform.py:13.title: Aggregate per station and day
etl/transform.py:13.text: groupby on four keys, select temp, then agg computes min, max, mean and count per group. reset_index turns the group keys back into columns: 12 stations over 2 days gives 24 rows.

etl/transform.py:15.title: Round the daily mean
etl/transform.py:15.text: Replaces the mean column in place with values rounded to 2 decimals.

etl/transform.py:21.title: Group daily means by region
etl/transform.py:21.text: A SeriesGroupBy over the mean column, keyed by region. Nothing is computed yet; it's evaluated by the transform calls on the next line.

etl/transform.py:22.title: Compute each row's z-score within its region
etl/transform.py:22.text: transform("mean") and transform("std") broadcast each region's statistic back to every row, so the subtraction and division are row-aligned. A zero std is replaced with NaN to avoid dividing by zero.

etl/transform.py:23.title: Keep rows far from their region
etl/transform.py:23.text: Filters to rows whose absolute z-score exceeds ANOMALY_Z (1.4). copy() returns an independent frame rather than a view of summary. 3 rows are flagged, all from Mesa Top.

etl/load.py:8.title: Make sure the output folder exists
etl/load.py:8.text: makedirs with exist_ok=True creates the folder if needed and does nothing if it already exists. In safe mode, codestory created it in the sandbox instead.

etl/load.py:10.title: Write the CSV report
etl/load.py:10.text: to_csv writes the 24-row summary; index=False leaves out pandas' row index. Safe mode redirected the file to the sandbox.

etl/load.py:15.title: Open the stations database for writing
etl/load.py:15.text: Same context-manager pattern as on read: the with block commits the transaction when it exits without an error.

etl/load.py:16.title: Clear the table on a full refresh
etl/load.py:16.text: Runs the DELETE only when --full-refresh was passed. It was, so the table is emptied before the insert; without it, rows would be appended to the existing ones.

etl/load.py:18.title: Insert the summary rows
etl/load.py:18.text: astype(str) converts the date objects to text (SQLite has no date type), then to_sql with if_exists="append" inserts the 24 rows using executemany on the connection. Safe mode applied this to the database copy.

main.py:38.title: Alert only when there's something to report
main.py:38.text: The condition is truthy when anomalies is non-empty and --no-alerts wasn't passed. len() is used because a DataFrame's truth value is ambiguous and would raise.

etl/load.py:23.title: Build the alert payload
etl/load.py:23.text: A JSON-serialisable dict: the count, and the flagged rows as a list of records via to_dict(orient="records").

etl/load.py:25.title: Post the alert to the webhook
etl/load.py:25.text: requests.post sends the payload as JSON with a 10-second timeout. Safe mode blocked the request and returned a fake 200, so nothing left the machine.
